description: An exploration of how businesses exchange information internally and externally, covering the communication process, types and channels of communication, barriers, qualities of effective communication, and the role of ICT in Tanzanian commerce.

mcq.questionText: What is the most accurate meaning of communication in business?

options.text: The buying and selling of goods between traders
The process of exchanging information, ideas and messages between people to reach a common understanding
The storage of business records in a warehouse
The transport of goods from producer to consumer

mcq.explanation: Communication is the two-way process of transmitting and receiving information, ideas and messages so that the sender and receiver share a common understanding.

mcq.questionText: In the communication process, the person who originates and sends the message is called the:
mcq.explanation: The sender (also called the source or encoder) is the party who initiates the communication by creating and transmitting the message.

mcq.questionText: Converting an idea into words, symbols or signals before sending is known as:
mcq.explanation: Encoding is the stage where the sender translates ideas into a form (words, symbols or gestures) that can be transmitted to the receiver.

mcq.questionText: The response that the receiver gives back to the sender to show the message was understood is called:
mcq.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's reaction or reply, which completes the communication cycle and confirms whether the message was understood.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of internal business communication?

options.text: A letter sent to a supplier in Dar es Salaam
A memo circulated between departments of the same company
An advertisement placed on television for customers
An invoice issued to a customer

mcq.explanation: Internal communication takes place within the organisation, such as memos exchanged between departments. Letters to suppliers, adverts and invoices are external communication.

mcq.questionText: A written communication used within an organisation to pass brief information between officers is a:
mcq.explanation: A memorandum (memo) is a short internal note used to convey information, instructions or reminders between staff in the same organisation.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a form of non-verbal communication?
mcq.explanation: Non-verbal communication uses gestures, body language, facial expressions and signs rather than spoken or written words.

mcq.questionText: The document that states the items to be discussed in a meeting, prepared and circulated before the meeting, is the:
mcq.explanation: An agenda is the list of topics to be discussed at a meeting, drawn up in advance so members can prepare; minutes are written afterwards as a record.

mcq.questionText: The written record of what was discussed and decided in a meeting is called:
mcq.explanation: Minutes are the official written record of proceedings, resolutions and decisions made during a meeting.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is NOT a quality of effective business communication?
mcq.explanation: Effective communication should be clear, concise, courteous, correct and complete. Ambiguity (vagueness) is a weakness, not a quality.

mcq.questionText: A single message sent to many people at once, such as a notice from management to all staff, is best described as a:
mcq.explanation: A circular is a written message duplicated and distributed to many recipients at the same time to convey the same information.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a barrier to effective communication?

options.text: Use of difficult technical jargon the receiver cannot understand

mcq.explanation: Using jargon or language the receiver does not understand is a semantic barrier that prevents the message from being understood correctly.

mcq.questionText: Communication that follows the official chain of command and recognised procedures of an organisation is called:
mcq.explanation: Formal communication moves through official channels and follows the organisation's established lines of authority and rules.

mcq.questionText: Which means of communication allows a written document to be transmitted electronically as an exact copy over telephone lines?
mcq.explanation: A fax (facsimile) machine scans a document and sends an exact reproduction to another fax machine through telephone lines.

mcq.questionText: What is the main advantage of using email over an ordinary posted letter for business communication in Tanzania?

options.text: It is slower and more expensive
It delivers messages almost instantly and at very low cost
It always requires a physical signature

mcq.explanation: Email transmits messages and attachments almost instantly to any part of the world at a very low cost, unlike postal letters which are slow.

fib.questionText: The two-way process of exchanging information and ideas to reach a common understanding is called _____.
fib.explanation: Communication is the process of transmitting and receiving messages so that meaning is shared between parties.

fib.questionText: In the communication process, translating an idea into words or symbols is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Encoding is the stage where the sender converts a thought into a transmittable form such as words or symbols.

fib.questionText: The interpretation of a received message by the receiver is called _____.
fib.explanation: Decoding is the process by which the receiver interprets and makes sense of the message that was sent.

fib.questionText: The medium or path through which a message travels from sender to receiver is the _____.
fib.explanation: The channel (or medium) is the route, such as a letter, telephone or email, used to carry the message.

fib.questionText: Communication that takes place between an organisation and outside parties such as customers and suppliers is called _____ communication.
fib.explanation: External communication links the business with parties outside it, such as customers, suppliers, banks and government.

fib.questionText: A short written note used to pass brief information between officers within the same organisation is a _____.
fib.explanation: A memo (memorandum) is an internal written communication used for brief messages and reminders among staff.

fib.questionText: The official written record of what was discussed and decided at a meeting is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Minutes record the proceedings, decisions and resolutions of a meeting for future reference.

fib.questionText: Anything that interferes with or distorts a message during transmission is generally called _____.
fib.explanation: Noise is any interference (physical, semantic or psychological) that hinders the clear transmission of a message.

fib.questionText: The quality of effective communication that means using as few words as possible without losing meaning is _____.
fib.explanation: Conciseness means expressing the message briefly and to the point, avoiding unnecessary words.

fib.questionText: The use of computers, the internet and mobile phones to send and receive business information is summarised by the abbreviation _____.
fib.explanation: ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology, which plays a major role in fast, modern business communication.

tf.questionText: Communication is a one-way process that does not require any feedback.
tf.explanation: Communication is a two-way process; feedback is needed to confirm that the message was received and understood.

tf.questionText: A business letter sent to a supplier is an example of external communication.
tf.explanation: A supplier is outside the organisation, so a letter to a supplier is external communication.

tf.questionText: Body language and facial expressions are forms of non-verbal communication.
tf.explanation: Non-verbal communication conveys meaning through gestures, posture and facial expressions rather than words.

tf.questionText: An agenda is prepared after a meeting to record the decisions made.
tf.explanation: An agenda is prepared before a meeting to list items for discussion; the record of decisions made afterwards is the minutes.

tf.questionText: Email allows business messages and attachments to be sent quickly and cheaply over the internet.
tf.explanation: Email is a fast, low-cost electronic channel that can carry text and file attachments worldwide.

tf.questionText: Using technical jargon that the receiver does not understand improves communication.
tf.explanation: Unfamiliar jargon is a semantic barrier; it confuses the receiver and reduces effectiveness.

tf.questionText: Informal communication often spreads through unofficial channels such as the grapevine.
tf.explanation: Informal communication does not follow official lines; the grapevine is a common informal network among staff.

tf.questionText: A circular is a message addressed to only one specific person.
tf.explanation: A circular is duplicated and sent to many recipients at the same time, not to a single person.

tf.questionText: Clarity, courtesy and correctness are among the qualities of effective business communication.
tf.explanation: Effective communication should be clear, courteous, correct, concise and complete (the C's of communication).

tf.questionText: A telephone is a means of oral (verbal) communication.
tf.explanation: The telephone carries the spoken word, making it a means of oral or verbal communication.

summary.questionText: State the meaning of business communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Business communication is the process of exchanging information, ideas, messages and instructions between people within and outside a business organisation in order to reach a common understanding and achieve business goals.
summary.explanation: It captures the core idea of a shared exchange of information aimed at achieving business objectives.

summary.questionText: List the main elements of the communication process.
summary.correctAnswer: The main elements are the sender, the message, encoding, the channel (medium), the receiver, decoding and feedback.
summary.explanation: These are the standard components of the communication cycle from origination of a message to feedback.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between internal and external communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Internal communication takes place among people within the same organisation, such as memos and meetings between departments, while external communication takes place between the organisation and outside parties such as customers, suppliers, banks and government.
summary.explanation: The distinction is based on whether the parties are inside or outside the organisation.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between verbal and non-verbal communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Verbal communication uses words, either spoken (oral) such as meetings and telephone calls, or written such as letters and reports, while non-verbal communication conveys meaning without words, through gestures, body language, facial expressions and signs.
summary.explanation: Verbal relies on words; non-verbal relies on signs, gestures and expressions.

summary.questionText: Mention four examples of written business communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Examples include business letters, memos, reports, notices, circulars, emails, agendas and minutes.
summary.explanation: Any four of these recognised written forms are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Identify four means or channels of communication used in business.
summary.correctAnswer: Means of communication include postal services (letters), the telephone, fax, email, the internet and social media.
summary.explanation: These are the common channels through which business messages are transmitted.

summary.questionText: State four barriers to effective communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Barriers include the use of difficult language or jargon, noise and physical distractions, poor choice of channel, lack of feedback, differences in language, and emotional or attitudinal problems between sender and receiver.
summary.explanation: Any four valid barriers (semantic, physical, psychological or organisational) are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Suggest four ways of overcoming barriers to communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Barriers can be overcome by using simple and clear language, choosing the appropriate channel, reducing noise and distractions, encouraging feedback, listening attentively, and ensuring the message is complete and well-timed.
summary.explanation: Any four practical measures that remove or reduce barriers are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Outline the qualities of effective business communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Effective communication should be clear, concise, courteous, correct and complete, and should also be timely and use the appropriate channel.
summary.explanation: These are commonly referred to as the C's of effective communication.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of ICT in modern business communication.
summary.correctAnswer: ICT enables fast and low-cost transmission of information through email, the internet, mobile phones and social media; it allows businesses to reach customers and suppliers across distances, store and retrieve information easily, hold virtual meetings, and improve speed, accuracy and efficiency in communication.
summary.explanation: ICT improves speed, reach, cost and accuracy of business communication in Tanzania and worldwide.

hoq.questionText: A wholesaler in Mwanza urgently needs written confirmation of a price quotation from a manufacturer in Dar es Salaam, and the document must arrive within minutes carrying the supplier's stamp and signature for the records. Which channel is MOST suitable?

options.text: Ordinary surface mail through the post office
A fax or scanned email of the signed and stamped quotation
A notice posted on the company notice board

hoq.explanation: The need for speed plus a written, signed and stamped document points to fax or a scanned email, which deliver an exact copy almost instantly. Post is too slow, a phone call leaves no signed record, and a notice board does not reach the wholesaler.

hoq.questionText: During a staff meeting at a Dar es Salaam firm, the manager speaks but workers keep misunderstanding instructions because of a noisy generator outside, the manager's heavy use of technical terms, and workers being afraid to ask questions. Which combination of barriers is present?
hoq.explanation: The generator noise is a physical barrier, the technical terms are a semantic (language) barrier, and the workers' fear of asking questions is a psychological barrier, so all three types are present together.

hoq.questionText: A Tanzanian company wants to announce a new product to thousands of potential customers nationwide instantly, at low cost, while also allowing customers to respond and ask questions. Which approach BEST achieves this?

options.text: Sending an individually typed business letter to each customer by post
Pinning a single notice on the office notice board
Using social media and the internet, which reach many people instantly and allow two-way feedback
Making separate telephone calls to each customer one by one

hoq.explanation: Social media and the internet (ICT) reach large numbers of people instantly and cheaply and permit immediate two-way feedback, unlike posted letters, a single notice or one-by-one phone calls, which are slow, limited in reach or costly in time.
